newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down on correction.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed down on Tuesday on a correction after rises over the past two sessions, with sentiment hurt by sharp losses in the A share market, traders said.
The B index fell 0.507 points or 0.81 percent to 62.381 points, on volume of 15 million shares worth $7.0 million against $8.2 million on Monday.
Shanghai's A share index tumbled 2.38 percent or 23.054 points to 947.261 on volume of 277 million shares worth 2.5 billion yuan, down from Monday's 3.1 billion yuan.
Brokers said selling in property developer Lujiazui on concerns about its 1996 results depressed the market and falls on the domestic A share market worsened market sentiment further.

Shanghai's A shares were down sharply on the news that the China Agribusiness Trust & Investment Corp, a major domestic investment firm, had been closed because of serious illegal and irregular business practices, brokers said.
Lujiazui was the day's second most heavily traded share with 2.8 million shares changing hands. It fell $0.028 or 3.39 percent to $0.796.

"Domestic investors, who have dominated trading recently with overseas investors on the sidelines, have become cautious on uncertainties over the market, particularly given the resistance the index is meeting around the 63-point level," one broker said.
"The index will dip further in the short term to seek speculative institutional support around the 60-point level," a second broker said.
Hua Xin cement was the biggest loser on institutional unwinding selling on expectations of poor results, down $0.010 or 4.13 percent to $0.232 on volume of 734,100 shares.
Clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai was again the most active share and became the second biggest loser on profit-taking, falling $0.014 or 3.93 percent to $0.342 on volume of 3.2 million shares.
Of 43 B shares, 40 traded with 22 down, nine flat and nine up.
In the A share market, the SSE 30 blue-chip index dipped 47.686 points or 1.94 percent to 2408.783 points.
Iron and steel producer Chengdu Gongyi was the biggest decliner on institutional selling, falling 0.39 yuan or 6.02 percent to 6.09 yuan on volume of 6.7 million shares.
